* checking foreign function calls ... WARNING
Foreign function call(s) with ?PACKAGE? argument in a base package:
   .C("find_interv_vec", ..., PACKAGE = "base")

This is not part of the R API and will be removed shortly.

Your uses of it are in any case incorrect and dangerous (e.g. length() 
does not need to return an integer and might be NA: see its help page).

Please remove this from your code (and be aware that such calls are seen 
as prime facie evidence of copying from the R sources, which you have 
not acknowledged).

messages.subject: .C calls in CRAN packages to other packages not depended on
messages.subject_clean: .C calls in CRAN packages to other packages not depended on
messages.body_plain:
This concerns packages aroma.core, npRmpi, pairwiseCI and timeDate.

As you can see from the R-devel checks at

http://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-devel-linux-x86_64-gcc-fedora/<pkgname>-00check.html

you are making .C calls to another package which is not mentioned in the 
DESCRIPTION file and hence need not even be installed on the system your 
package is running on.

In any case, using non-API interfaces in other packages is unsafe, and 
at C level is an all too easy way to crash the R session the user of 
your package is running (and because that was happening too often, these 
checks were added).  If you really need a low-level API, please 
negotiate with the other package maintainer to provide one.

Please fix this (and other issues showing in those checks) as soon as 
possible.

-- 
Brian D. Ripley,                  ripley at stats.ox.ac.uk

On Tue, 7 Aug 2012, Yohan Chalabi wrote:

>
> On Aug 1, 2012, at 2:52 PM, Prof Brian Ripley wrote:
>
>> We see in R CMD check in current R-devel
>>
>> * checking foreign function calls ... WARNING
>> Foreign function call(s) with ?PACKAGE? argument in a base package:
>>  .C("find_interv_vec", ..., PACKAGE = "base")
>>
>> This is not part of the R API and will be removed shortly.
>>
>
> Thanks for pointing out that find_interv_vec will has been removed from R-dev. We will make the due changes in the timeSeries package.
>
>> Your uses of it are in any case incorrect and dangerous (e.g. length() does not need to return an integer and might be NA: see its help page).
>>
>> Please remove this from your code (and be aware that such calls are seen as prime facie evidence of copying from the R sources, which you have not acknowledged).
>
> It is mentioned in the source code that we prefer to call the 
> underlining C routine of findInterval(). Moreover, we only call the 
> C routine and we have not copied the code in findInterval().

But you did: you copied to write

     .C("find_interv_vec", xt = pos, n = length(pos), x = ipos,
        nx = nx, FALSE, FALSE, i, DUP = FALSE, NAOK = TRUE,
        PACKAGE = "base")

which are not otherwise documented.  You need to acknowledge that this 
is an edited copy of R-core's code.  And most of the parts which 
differ from the current findInterval() are in fact wrong: nx need not 
be of type integer and could be NA, for example.  And if it were 
called with the wrong type, the crash would be attributed to R's 
internals and not to your error.

-- 
Brian D. Ripley,                  ripley at stats.ox.ac.uk

messages.subject: VaR constraint in fPortfolio
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

thank you for contributing to R with you package fPortfolio.
I am looking at it and have a question for you.

1/ I would like to maximise the return of a portfolio, over the following
constraints:
   * each asset cannot be allocated more than a cap
   * each group of asset cannot be allocated more than a cap (gross or net
sum of weights)
   * VaR or CVaR constraint on group of assets
Is it possible using fPortfolio?

2/ I understand that we can setup group constraints in terms of weight cap.
But can we do the same for VaR or CVaR constraints? Let's suppose that I
have chosen CVaR as risk measure in the model. How will the constraint be
defined?

Thank you for you help. I read carefully the help for the package but could
not manage to understand precisely how to use the functions.

Xavier
